title: transcript/1 — the viewer's lived story: delivered narration, newest first, cursor-paginated
description: GET /worlds/{w}/transcript. Viewer-scoped. Unlike every other read surface this is a RECORD, not a projection: the prose a model wrote once cannot be recomputed from world state. Entries are returned exactly as they were delivered and are NEVER retro-labelled — an entry written before the viewer learned a name still says 'the muscle by the bar' after he learns 'Jonas', because a memory of an experience is itself a perception. History begins when the feature shipped; beats played before it are not stored and are not fabricated.

entries.description: Newest first. One entry per narrated beat.

entry_no.description: Monotonic per-row ordering handle and the pagination cursor. Not domain time: several entries can share one tick, so a tick cannot order or paginate them.

tick.description: The in-world tick the beat started at (B-5 logical time). For display and grouping, never for ordering.

stated.description: The player's own input, stored RAW — never parsed, never reformatted. Null when he typed nothing (a continue press), which is a different fact from an empty string.

journey.description: The journey block as delivered, or null when the beat had none — the marker the frontend needs to render travel in history the way it rendered it live.

segments.description: The delivered narration, in order — the SAME message shape a live beat_frame/4 narration frame carries, so history and live prose render through one path.

speaker_label.description: The label AS IT WAS at the time — deliberately frozen, never re-resolved against present knowledge.

text.description: Prose. The whole segment for narration and action; for speech, the staging around the line, possibly empty.

quote.description: The verbatim spoken words. Non-empty exactly when kind is speech; null otherwise.

next_before.description: Cursor for the next (older) page: pass as ?before=. Null means this page reached the beginning of the story — page until null rather than inferring the end from a short page.
